newsitem.title: USA: US spot propane prices sag amid mild weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot propane prices sag amid mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices, particularly in the midcontinent hub of Conway, Kansas, sagged Monday in quiet pre-holiday talk amid rather warm temperatures coming on the heels of rather cool weather, traders said.

Prompt December propane fell by over over 5.00 cents a gallon, with one trader pegging prices in the 65/67 cents a gallon range. Barrels for early January delivery were pegged in the 60 to 61 cents range.
Some traders said another bearish factor at play was TET Pipeline's allocation program, which was stranding volumes at the Mount Belvieu, Texas terminus of the TET system.
Prices at the Mont Belvieu hub were indeed lower, due in part to the warm weather and perhaps the allocation, though not as sharply as in Kansas.
December propane stood at 49.00 t0 49.25 cents a gallon.
Also, some traders said November inventory data expected Monday from the American Petroleum Institute appeared to be delayed.
Traders noted trading volumes were light ahead of the New Year's Day Holiday, which will close the NYMEX early on Tuesday at 1300 EST/1800 GMT, and close it entirely on Wednesday.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
